data.body:
PLAN CORRECTED A SECOND TIME. Review #2 BLOCKED with four findings; all four were right, and the most
important one INVERTS this story's framing.

FINDING: my proposed enforcement mechanism could not work. I wrote that a transport missing a member
should 'fail an isinstance check at construction'. But TicketTransport is declared
'class TicketTransport(Protocol)' with NO @runtime_checkable — so isinstance against it raises
TypeError rather than returning False. Verified directly:

    TypeError: Instance and class checks can only be used with @runtime_checkable protocols

I had assumed it was runtime_checkable because Backend and the capability protocols are. The plan now
adds the decorator explicitly and names WHERE the assertion runs (the backend factories), which was
the separate COH/E1 finding — the AC promised a construction-time check that no section located.

THE BIG ONE: 'eleven would raise AttributeError' was FACTUALLY WRONG, and wrong in the direction that
matters. I classified every call site by whether an enclosing try swallows Exception:

    propagates (crashes):        2   get_issue_by_rest, set_reporter
    swallowed at EVERY site:     7   delete_issue_link, get_comments, get_issue_links,
                                     set_issue_property, set_parent, validate_assignee_exists,
                                     get_parent_map (hasattr-guarded)
    MIXED (crash some, swallowed elsewhere): 3   delete_issue, remove_label, set_entity_property

So a DC deployment does NOT mostly crash. It mostly APPEARS TO CONVERGE while quietly not syncing
comments, links, parents, issue properties, or validating assignees. set_entity_property is swallowed
at 2 of its 3 sites and crashes at the third — which is the ONLY reason any of this was ever
discovered. The crash was the LUCKY case.

CONSEQUENCE, and why this changes the story rather than just correcting a number: 'no AttributeError'
is the WRONG acceptance bar. It is already true at most sites, and true for the wrong reason. Fixing
only the crash would yield a GREEN live run with every silent gap intact — strictly worse than today,
because the green run would then be read as proof the capability works. The ACs now require asserting
each member is PRESENT, not merely that nothing raised.

That is the same trap as the completion-verifier lesson from earlier this session and the
half-fix landmine in J7: an absence of errors is not evidence of function. Three times now this epic
has produced a variant of it.
